lines.speaker: SENIOR COUNSEL
lines.text: No, no, no. Delete that paragraph. The application was dismissed, not disposed. Start again.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The wording in yesterday's order was disposed, sir.

lines.speaker: SENIOR COUNSEL
lines.text: Yesterday's order was mine. This one is also mine.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Let me finish the citations. I can sit inside until lunch.

lines.speaker: SENIOR COUNSEL
lines.text: You can wait outside until I call. My client is coming.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I have typed six pages already.

lines.speaker: SENIOR COUNSEL
lines.text: And you have been paid for six pages. Please close the door from the other side.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Fifteen years earlier, the bar council had struck Morris off. He still entered chambers every morning. He simply entered carrying typing paper.
lines.sfx_cue: door opening onto crowded court corridor

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Move away from the chamber door. Advocates on the left, litigants near the railing.
lines.sfx_cue: court corridor voices and shuffling files

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I am attached to this chamber.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Then your chair must also be attached. Go and wait on it.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CORRIDOR
lines.text: He says attached. Maybe he is the stapler.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The record will show who knows the work here.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: The record shows one typist blocking a corridor.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Sir... sir, please. Are you hearing urgent matters today?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Who told you to come here?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: The registry sent me upstairs. Upstairs sent me down. I have been going up and down since ten fifteen.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: What is the matter?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: My mother's room, sir. The landlord locked it. Her medicines are inside.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You have an advocate?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: He wants twelve hundred rupees before he reads the file. I have... I have four hundred and sixty.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then find legal aid.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: They gave me a token. Sixty-eight. The board is still showing twenty-three.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I did not ask for your token number.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: No, sir. Sorry, sir.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Do not trouble him. Can't you see he has been sent out to wait?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Sent out... from the chamber?

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Yes. With the other furniture.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Enough.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Certainly, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Let me see the file.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: The landlord says the agreement ended on the first. My mother says he took three months in advance. There is no receipt.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And the lock was changed today?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: At nine. She is sitting outside on the landing.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: This affidavit has no verification. This application asks for final relief as interim relief. Who drafted it?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: A man near the photocopy shop. Sir, can it be heard?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Not like this.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Then tell me how. Please. I will write exactly what you say.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Stand up first.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: No, sir. Not until you agree.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: People are watching.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Let them watch.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Sir, hear the case.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Sir, hear the case. Just once. My mother is still sitting outside that locked room.
lines.sfx_cue: crowded court corridor, files thudding on bench

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Take your hands away from my feet.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Say you will hear it.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I am not hearing anything. Stand up.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Your lordship, shall we clear the corridor for this historic sitting?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You have shouted enough for one morning.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: And you have been promoted quickly for one morning.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Come with me.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Inside the chamber?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. The copying room.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Listen carefully. This is only advice. You will not call it an order.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Yes, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You will not tell anyone I heard a case.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: No, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And stop calling me sir every second.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Yes... sorry.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Give me the landlord's notice.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Here. He wrote that we abandoned the room. My mother has slept there for nine years.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The notice gives seven days. When was it delivered?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Yesterday afternoon.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then he changed the lock before his own period expired.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Can you write that?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I can write many things. Whether a fool obeys the paper is a different question.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Morris fed one clean sheet into the machine. His fingers found the form they had typed ten thousand times for other men.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Upon perusal of the application... no. Upon perusal of the material placed on record.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: What material?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your file. Do not interrupt the record.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Sorry.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It appears that possession was disturbed during the subsistence of the notice period.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Will he understand this?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: He will understand the next sentence.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The respondent is directed to restore access forthwith, failing which further proceedings shall follow.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Further proceedings where?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Do you want your mother's key, or a lecture on jurisdiction?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: The key.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then let the sentence do its work.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: There is no stamp.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: A stamp impresses people who cannot read. Your landlord can read.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: And the signature?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The signature tells him someone is prepared to continue.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Prepared as what?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Give me the pen.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Presiding officer.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Sir... which office?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Do not ask a question when you are afraid of its answer.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That afternoon, Irfan carried the page to the landlord's hardware shop.
lines.sfx_cue: metal shop shutter rattling, traffic nearby

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: What is this?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: A direction to restore possession forthwith.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: From which court? There is no case number.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Read the last line.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Further proceedings shall follow.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Who signed it?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: The officer hearing the matter.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Hearing it where?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: You can ask him yourself. I will tell him you refused.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: There is no need to become dramatic. I changed the lock to protect the property.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: My mother is outside.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Take the spare key. I am obeying under protest.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: And the three months' advance?

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: You people learn one legal phrase and become advocates.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: The notice says you received it.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Six thousand rupees.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I will deduct electricity.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: There is no electricity bill pending.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Fine. Six thousand. Sign here and leave my shop.
lines.sfx_cue: cash notes counted on metal counter

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The page had no case number, no seal and no court behind it. The landlord paid all six thousand rupees.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: He obeyed every line.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Lower your voice.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: He returned the key. He returned the advance. My mother touched this paper to her forehead.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I told you, it was advice.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Advice does not return six thousand rupees.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then what do you think it was?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: A judgment.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Do not use words you do not understand.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: I understand what opened the door.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And what have you brought in that envelope?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Four hundred and sixty rupees. Everything I had yesterday.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Take it back.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Then call it filing fees.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: There was no filing.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: There will be now.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Sir, Irfan said you hear urgent property matters.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: We brought our files.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: And they brought their fees.
lines.sfx_cue: two cash envelopes placed beside the files

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Sir, my brother sold our father's sewing machines without asking me. I need an order before he sells the shop.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: Mine is a salary matter. Three months unpaid. Irfan said you can finish it quickly.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I have not accepted either matter.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: They came because the first order worked.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: That was not an order.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Then write me the same kind of not-order.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: I can pay five hundred now. Another five hundred after recovery.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: This is a public canteen. Put the money away.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Where should we put it? Irfan said your office is upstairs.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: I said he works upstairs. I did not say he has an office.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Enough. Both of you, wait until evening. Bring every agreement, receipt and notice you possess.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Where will you hear us?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You will be informed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Morris did not take the envelopes in the canteen. He took them under the table, where dignity could pretend not to see.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Five days after Irfan touched his feet, Morris climbed the stairs above a tyre shop.
lines.sfx_cue: air wrench bursts, metal staircase creaking

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Mind the second step. It bends when heavy people use it.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You said the room had a separate entrance.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: It does. Nobody enters through the tyres unless they fall through the floor.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: There is grease on the wall.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: There is grease downstairs also. That is how a tyre shop earns money.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Clients must be able to wait outside.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: What clients? You said typing work.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Documentation. Consultations. Settlement of private disputes.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Advocate work?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Good. Advocates argue about rent. Typists pay it.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The room needs two tables, six chairs and a raised platform.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: A platform? Are you starting a dance class?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: A dais.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Same wood, more English.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Four thousand deposit. Two thousand per month. Electricity separate.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You told Irfan fifteen hundred.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: For typing. A dais costs five hundred extra because it sounds important.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Three thousand deposit. Seventeen hundred rent.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Three thousand deposit. Two thousand rent. I will wash the grease once.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And repair the second step.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: The step has survived twelve years. It can survive your clients.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Three thousand and five hundred deposit. Eighteen hundred rent. Today.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: You negotiate like an advocate.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Write the receipt.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Occupation?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Dispute resolution.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: That is not an occupation.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It is now.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: By noon, one carpenter had placed a second-hand dining table on a platform eight inches high.

lines.speaker: CARPENTER
lines.text: If you lean on the left side, the whole thing will salute you.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Brace it underneath.

lines.speaker: CARPENTER
lines.text: That costs two hundred more.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It costs nothing if you had built it straight.

lines.speaker: CARPENTER
lines.text: Straight wood costs more than crooked wood, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Do it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At two, a sign painter carried in a black board with gold letters.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: Arbitration and Dispute Resolution Forum. Exactly as written.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The word forum is smaller than the others.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: You paid for twenty-four letters. This has thirty-seven.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And the line below?

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: Presiding Officer. That is large enough to read from the tyre shop.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Make sir smaller.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: There is no sir on the board.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I said officer. Make officer smaller.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: You said— never mind. Give me fifty rupees for correction.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Hang it straight first.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: What is this board?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It states the work conducted here.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: You told me typing.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Documents will be typed.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Do police come for dispute resolution?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Only if tyres are sold without receipts.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Your board is very handsome, sir. Please conduct all resolutions upstairs.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That was the first time the owner called him sir. Morris paid the sign painter without bargaining.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: A dais? You bought a dais before buying groceries?
lines.sfx_cue: home door bolt sliding, steel plate set down

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: There is rice for three days.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: There is rice. There is no oil. There is no dal. But somewhere above a tyre shop, there is a dais.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It is an office expense.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Say the office name properly.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Arbitration and Dispute Resolution Forum.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Who appointed you to it?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Private parties appoint an arbitrator by consent.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Did these parties consent?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: They brought files and fees.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: That is not what I asked.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The record will reflect consent.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: What record?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The one I am creating.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: And who keeps this record?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: A clerk.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: You have a clerk now?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I will have one tomorrow.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: With whose salary?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The forum's fees.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Morris... look at me. Is this a court?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. It is a lawful private forum.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Then why does it need a dais?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Because people obey a raised table.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, I was told there is a clerk vacancy.
lines.sfx_cue: tyre compressor hiss, metal stairs creaking

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Who told you?

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: The sign painter. He is my mother's neighbour. He said you paid on time.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Have you worked in an office before?

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: No, sir. I finished twelfth standard. I can read English, type slowly and make tea quickly.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Tea is not part of the designation.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: There is a designation?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Registry clerk.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Registry... like a court registry?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Like a private forum registry.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Will I have to wear a uniform?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. Plain clothes. Clean file work. You will maintain the register and call matters by number.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: I don't... I have never called a matter.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Say, matter number one, parties to enter.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Matter number one, parties to enter.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Louder. People waiting near an air compressor must hear you.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Matter number one, parties to enter!

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Very respectable. Even my customers are frightened.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: What is the salary, sir?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Three thousand rupees per month. Paid on the last working day.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Three thousand... every month?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: If the register is correct.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: My father gets two thousand six hundred for night security.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your father's salary is not before this forum.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sorry, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Read this appointment acknowledgment. Sign at the bottom.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: It says I certify the proceedings recorded by me.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: That is standard language.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: What proceedings?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The matters you call. The appearances. The documents filed.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: And if I spell something wrong?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You correct it before signing.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: My mother will not believe this. Nobody in our family has had a desk job.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then give her something respectable to believe.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At four thirty, Sarika opened a new register. Morris wrote one on the first page and two on the second.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Matter number one, parties to enter!
lines.sfx_cue: door opening, tyre shop noise beneath

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Do I stand or sit?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Sit. Place the sale receipt on record.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: There was no receipt. My brother took cash.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then how do you know the machines were sold?

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: The shop is empty.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Sarika, record that the machines are absent from the shared premises.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Absent from shared premises.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Sir, will you stop him selling the shop also?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: First, the other party receives notice. Then the other party speaks.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: What if he refuses to come?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then his refusal enters the record before he does.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Yes, sir.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Matter number two, parties to enter!

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: Only I have come. My employer sent nobody.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Did your employer receive written demand?

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: Three letters. He tore one in front of me.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You will file copies of the other two.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: Will you order payment today?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: I was told this is fast.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Fast is not the same as foolish. Notice in three days. Reply in seven. Hearing on the eighth day.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: And if he pays before then?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You inform the registry. The matter closes.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: The registry means me?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The registry means the office. You are its clerk.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Yes, sir. Sorry, sir.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: How much filing fee?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Five hundred rupees. Sarika will issue the receipt.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: I issue receipts also?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: From today.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At five ten, both men left carrying numbered notices. Sarika remained behind, tracing the gold letters on the nameplate with one finger.
lines.sfx_cue: metal stairs descending, room door settling

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, should I lock the register in a cupboard?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Tomorrow. We will purchase one with the next filing fee.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: And if somebody comes without an appointment?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Nobody knows this address yet.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: The two matters are finished for today.

lines.speaker: STRANGER
lines.text: I am not one of the two.

lines.speaker: STRANGER
lines.text: I need the presiding officer.
lines.sfx_cue: heavy file dropped on registry desk

beat_sheet.what_happened: Fifteen years after being struck off, Morris typed another man's order and was sent out of the chamber to wait.

state_changes.fact: He is publicly reduced from legal professional to paid typist.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Irfan mistook Morris for an official who could hear his urgent housing dispute, and Morris examined the file without correcting him.

state_changes.fact: He believes Morris has authority to hear urgent matters.
He experiences public deference for the first time in years.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Irfan touched Morris's feet and asked him to hear the case.

state_changes.fact: He is directly invited to exercise judicial authority again.
He places his mother's housing dispute in Morris's hands.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Morris called his intervention advice, typed a direction in judicial form and signed it as presiding officer.

state_changes.fact: He creates his first signed direction for a private litigant.
He receives a paper intended to compel restoration of the room.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Irfan presented Morris's signed page, and the landlord restored the key and paid six thousand rupees without court proceedings.

state_changes.fact: His mother regains access and the full advance payment.
It produces voluntary compliance despite lacking a seal or case number.

beat_sheet.what_happened: A copy of Morris's first signed direction remained preserved with the housing papers after payment.

state_changes.fact: A discoverable copy survives after the dispute is resolved.

beat_sheet.note: No cast character observes where the retained copy is stored, leaving its future chain of discovery open.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Irfan returned to Morris with two more men, their files and their fees.

state_changes.fact: His one intervention becomes a potential paid practice.
